problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation:

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{4}+{20}^{∘})=2.
$$

The general solution of this equation is

$$
x={a}^{∘}+1\,{440}^{∘}\cdot n,\,x=1\,{120}^{∘}+1\,{440}^{∘}\cdot n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$

Consider the following trigonometric equation:

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x)=-2
$$

The general solution of this equation is

$$
x=\frac{2\pi }{9}+\frac{2\pi n}{3},\,x=a\pi +\frac{2\pi n}{3},
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $[0,\frac{2}{3}).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
3x=\frac{2\pi }{3}+2\pi n,\,3x=\frac{4\pi }{3}+2\pi n.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+2\pi n, & \,3x & =\frac{4\pi }{3}+2\pi n \\ x & =\frac{2\pi }{9}+\frac{2\pi n}{3}, & \,x & =\frac{4\pi }{9}+\frac{2\pi n}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have that $a=\frac{4}{9}.$
